title: Crop Insurance Servicing Desk Guidance on Unpaid Premium, Interest and Termination for Indebtedness
content:
**Rule.** Crop Insurance premium and fees not paid within the product's interest-free period of calendar days after the billing date accrue simple interest at the product's monthly interest percentage for each month or part of a month from the billing date, charged at each month end. Payments are applied to interest, then fees, then premium. A policy with any premium, fee or interest still unpaid on the termination date of the year after the crop year is terminated for indebtedness and, where the product makes a termination for indebtedness a cause of ineligibility, the member is ineligible for all federal crop insurance until the debt is paid.

The product's figures are the same at every plan and coverage level: an interest-free period of 30 calendar days after the billing date and simple interest of 1.25% per month or part of a month.

## Input, judgement, output

| What the member's account shows | Judgement | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Premium and fees paid within 30 calendar days after the billing date | paid within the interest-free period | no interest accrues |
| Premium or fees still unpaid after 30 calendar days | not paid within the period | simple interest of 1.25% for each month or part of a month from the billing date, charged at each month end |
| Any premium, fee or interest still unpaid on the termination date of the year after the crop year | unpaid on the termination date | the policy is terminated for indebtedness and the member is ineligible for all federal crop insurance until the debt is paid |

The number of days that matters is the count of calendar days the billed premium has remained unpaid, from the premium billing date to the date considered. Each interest charge appears on the account as its own entry dated the last day of the month charged; each payment appears with the date received and its channel. A terminated policy moves from **active** to **terminated**, with the termination date recorded.

## Worked illustrations (hypothetical amounts)

**Simple interest.** On $1,000.00 of premium and fees left unpaid beyond the interest-free period, each month or part of a month from the billing date carries 1.25%, that is $12.50. Interest is simple: it is figured on the unpaid premium and fees alone, so three months or parts of months come to $37.50.

**Applying a payment.** A member owes $12.50 of interest, a $30.00 administrative fee and $500.00 of premium, and pays $100.00. The payment goes first to the $12.50 of interest, then to the $30.00 fee, and the remaining $57.50 to premium, which leaves $442.50 of premium owing.

**Termination.** For a hypothetical 2025 crop year the termination date falls in 2026. If $12.50 of interest alone is unpaid on that date, the policy has interest still unpaid on the termination date and is terminated for indebtedness.

## Points of judgement

- *Order of application.* A payment smaller than the interest owed is applied wholly to interest; fees are reached only once interest is paid, and premium only once fees are paid.
- *Ineligibility.* The ineligibility after a termination for indebtedness extends to all federal crop insurance and lasts until the debt is paid.
